author: fwyzard
body: **This is a draft PR, opened as a request for comments: it is not meant to be merged in its current form.** #### PR description: On machines with more than one NUMA node, a single job using all the cpus is slower than the same cpus split among one job per socket: the threads of a stream migrate between nodes, and the stream's data and the EventSetup products are read from remote memory. This PR adds `process.options.numaLocality` (default `False`). When it is enabled and the job's cpus span more than one NUMA node, it: - creates one TBB arena per NUMA domain, and assigns the framework threads, including the main thread, to the arenas in proportion to the number of cpus (hardware threads) available to the job in each domain; the threads of each arena are pinned to the cpus of its domain; the main thread joins the first arena in a slot reserved for it and, while it waits for the transitions, runs any task of that arena like the other threads; - assigns the streams to the NUMA domains in the same proportion, in contiguous blocks, and runs each event in the arena of its stream's domain; all the tasks spawned by the event stay in that arena; - starts each event through `numa::runInDomain()`: on the local queue of the reading thread if it already runs in the arena of the event's stream, otherwise in the queue of that arena; - constructs the per-stream objects (stream schedules, workers, event principals) on the node of their stream; - gives each domain its own copy of the EventSetup products, produced by a task running in the arena of that domain; `process.options.eventSetup.numaReplicatedRecords` and `numaExcludedRecords` restrict the replication to, or exclude from it, some records; - sets a local memory policy for the whole job (as `numactl --localalloc`), from `cmsRun` and `PythonEventProcessor` before the TBB worker threads are created; this also takes the job out of the kernel's automatic NUMA balancing; - makes the FastTimerService observe the per-domain arenas, so that their threads are registered and timed. It also warns about jobs that are not pinned and have fewer threads than cpus, and reports at the end of the job how many threads moved between arenas. Nothing changes if `numaLocality` is not enabled; if the job's cpus are all on one NUMA node, only the memory policy applies. #### Open points for discussion 1. **One option or one per feature.** `numaLocality` enables everything together. The pieces could be controlled separately instead, e.g. `process.options.numa = cms.untracked.PSet(arenas = ..., streamPlacement = ..., replicateEventSetup = ..., memoryPolicy = ...)`. 2. 3. **Setting the memory policy in the code.** The same policy can be set from outside the job with `numactl --localalloc`; this PR sets it in `cmsRun` and `PythonEventProcessor` when `numaLocality` is enabled. The impact on a "sane" machine is also very small, but it was observed to be very significant on a machine with a higher cost for the memory transfers across sockets. #### Known issues with the EventSetup implementation - EventSetup products are _produced- N times, one per NUMA domain. At least some of them could be produced _once_ on one NUMA domain and copied to the other domains: this may require a way to distinguish which ES products are safe to copy and which ones are not. - The `PoolDBESSource` (aka the GlobalTag) downloads and decompresses N copies of the payloads, one per NUMA domain. This is clearly not optimal and should be improved. - alpaka ESProducers create NM copies of their payloads in GPU memory (number of NUMA domains times the number of GPUs). A first fix is to make them create only one copy. A possible improvement would be to fill each GPU's single payload from a task running on the closest NUMA domain. Longer term the assignment of the streams, GPUs and NUMA domains needs to be investigated and improved significantly. - With EventSetup replication, `ESProductResolverProvider::initConcurrentIOVs()` receives the number of concurrent IOVs multiplied by the number of domains; producers that size per-IOV caches by it see the larger number. In general, the interplay between stream modules and NUMA domains should be revisited. #### Other known points: - The main thread reads the source, runs the global transitions and produces the non-replicated EventSetup products inside the first arena, so the first NUMA domain carries some more work than its share of streams. I don't think anything can be done about the global transitions. I the future the source (or at least some types of source) could maybe be made aware of the NUMA domains. - The FastTimerService finds the per-domain arenas through `edm::numa::StreamNumaDomains`, so `HLTrigger/Timer` now depends on `FWCore/Concurrency`. The arenas are created before the `preallocate` signal is emitted, so they could be passed to the services with it, through `SystemBounds`, which would remove that dependency. #### Measurements Run 3 HLT menu, CPU only, one job using all the cpus of the machine including SMT, threads = streams = cpus, jemalloc 5.4.0. Raw throughput in events per second, average sigma. The reference is two concurrent jobs, one per socket, on the same cpus. All measurements include the service rework of #52158; the "#52158 only" column comes from an earlier set on IB 2026-10-19 (4 repetitions), the others from IB 2026-10-20. | machine | #52158 only | + this PR without the memory policy | + memory policy | two jobs, one per socket | |---|---|---|---|---| | 2 EPYC 9655 (2 96 cores) | 771.6 4.0 | 813.1 6.0 (26 reps) | 818.0 1.9 (26 reps) | 843.9 0.3 | | 2 EPYC 9534 (2 64 cores, NPS2) | 396.5 4.3 | 422.2 1.9 (24 reps) | 425.1 1.5 (24 reps) | 443.8 0.3 | | 2 EPYC 9965 (2 192 cores) | 488 13 | 754 349 (3 reps) | 1024 95 (21 reps) | 1304 2 | With this PR the single job reaches 97% (9655) and 96% (9534) of the two per-socket jobs. The 9965 machine has a known platform issue (a BIOS update is pending) that makes its full-machine results unstable; there the memory policy removes most of the instability, together with most of the job's kernel time. The variant that starts the events through `numa::runInDomain()` was chosen over enqueuing every event into its arena; the two are equal within the uncertainties (+0.2 0.2% on the 9655 and on the 9534). An (ongoing) scan shows a measurable gain on top of #52158: #### PR validation: Unit tests of FWCore/Concurrency, FWCore/ServiceRegistry, FWCore/Framework, FWCore/ParameterSet, FWCore/PythonFramework, FWCore/TestProcessor and HLTrigger/Timer pass. The HLT throughput measurements above ran with `numaLocality` enabled on the three machines; with it disabled the framework behaves as before.
title: [RFC] Keep the work and data of each stream on one NUMA node
